notes:
RECONSTRUCTED FROM PHOTOS — NOT A VERIFIED NETLIST.
Function: BLE motion + heading tag. nRF52832 reads a 6-axis IMU (U8) and an HP5883 magnetometer over one I²C bus (mag 0x0D, IMU 0x6A with SDO low), wakes on IMU_INT1 / IMU_INT2 / MAG_DRDY, reports charge state (CHG) and battery level (VBAT_AIN, 2:1 divider), button on BTN, programmed over the 4 SWD pads.
Seen: nRF52832-QFAA SoC, USB-C (back), 3.7 V 100 mAh LiPo with its own protection board, tact switch SW2, 32 MHz crystal Y1, a second (32.768 kHz) crystal, HP5883 magnetometer, U8 (the only other IC — treated as the IMU, marking not legible), 4 SWD pads on the back, meander PCB antenna with L3 and C12, inductors L1 / L2 on the back.
Assumed: IMU part number and pin set, charger / LDO identity, all component values, which GPIO does what, pull-ups, divider, how L1 / L2 / L3 are used. Placeholder references: U1, U2, U4, U5, J1, J2, BT1, AE1 and the unnamed resistors / capacitors.
Not modelled: U3 (pad groups at the top edge), R2/R5/R16–R18, C24 and other small parts whose function could not be read.
Power (estimate): IMU ≈ 1 mA + mag ≈ 0.1 mA + nRF BLE average ≈ 0.2–0.5 mA → ≈ 1.5 mA streaming, ≈ 60 h on 100 mAh; far longer when the IMU sleeps and wakes on INT.
Verify with a meter and the datasheets before relying on any connection.

customParts.name: nRF52832-QFAA (functional)
customParts.desc: Nordic nRF52832 BLE SoC (QFN48 6×6), only the pins this board uses — marked N52832 QFAA E1 2225BZ
specs: ARM Cortex-M4F 64 MHz, BLE 5, 512 kB flash / 64 kB RAM
VDD 1.7–3.6 V (NOT directly from a 4.2 V LiPo)
32 MHz crystal on XC1/XC2, 32.768 kHz crystal on XL1/XL2
TWI on SDA/SCL, internal pull-ups available
SAADC input VBAT_AIN for the battery divider
customParts.notes: Functional symbol — pin numbers here are just the order in this list, NOT the QFN48 pin numbers. GPIO assignments (SDA, SCL, BTN, IMU_INT1/2, MAG_DRDY, CHG, VBAT_AIN) are assumed. Check the Nordic product specification before probing the real chip.

customParts.name: USB-C receptacle (power)
specs: 5.1 kΩ each to GND makes a sink (UFP)
customParts.notes: Seen on the back of the board at the top edge.

customParts.name: Li-ion charger SOT-23-5 (TP4054-class)
customParts.desc: Single-cell linear charger — assumed part (identity not read from the photos)
customParts.notes: ASSUMED. A 5-pin SMD IC sits next to the USB-C connector on the back; this is the usual part in that spot. Not modelled electrically in the simulation.

customParts.name: HP5883 magnetometer (QMC5883-class)
customParts.notes: Functional pin list, not package pin numbers. Support parts (4.7 µF on C1, 0.22 µF SETC–SETP, 0.1 µF decoupling) follow the QMC5883L application note.

customParts.name: 6-axis IMU (U8, accel + gyro)
customParts.desc: U8: 3-axis accelerometer + 3-axis gyroscope, I²C/SPI. Package marking not legible in the photos, so the exact part is not identified.
specs: I²C (CS high, SDO = address LSB) or SPI
customParts.notes: Typical pin set for this class of IMU (LSM6DS3 / BMI160 / ICM-426xx). Pin numbers are not package pin numbers. Identify the real part number and check its datasheet.

customParts.name: PCB trace antenna
customParts.desc: 2.4 GHz meander antenna etched on the board edge

customParts.name: SWD test pads
customParts.desc: Four round test pads on the back: clock, data, ground, VDD
customParts.notes: Pad order read from the back-side silkscreen; confirm which pad is which with a meter.
